newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps weaker except for firmer gasoline.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps weaker except for firmer gasoline.

text.p: European oil swaps were generally weaker on Monday bar stronger gasoline, which bucked the trend. Fuel oil lost $1 or so and Brent crude CFDs eased back a few cents while gasoline gained $3.
Dealers said gasoline's partial reversal of the heavy losses sustained late on Friday was backed by tight supplies in NWE and talk of low octane material being sought to take transatlantic.
August swaps tracked up to $190 with September $4 backwardated. August traded at $190.50.
Brent CFDs were marginally softer with July 21-25 pegged at -10 cents against September from -11/12 cents while July 28-August 1 was pegged at -5 cents compared with -3 cents.
August 4-8 was assessed at -10 cents against September from 02 cents and August 11-15 was talked around -15 cents compared with -10 cents.

An August 4-8 to August 11-15 role was done at +5 cents and July 18-22 was sold at October -27 cents. August 4-8 was concluded at September Brent -19 cents and August 25-29 went at -30 cents against October Brent.
July 28 to August 1 was sold at September -5 cents.
Heavy fuel swaps eased back $1 or so with August trading at $88.50. September was contangoed by $1 with October a further $1.50 stronger.
Dealers said interest was focused on east/west spread trading concern over Iraqi exports depressing the Med, prompting traders to buy the Far East.
Low sulphur fuel swaps were also easier, by $1-2 despite good U.S. physical demand.
Naphtha swaps eased back a touch with August pegged at $186-187 with September $3-4 backwardated. August traded at $186.00, traders said.
